ChatGPT is red-hot right now. Toutiao, WeChat Moments, Weibo: every big app keeps pushing it at us, right alongside plot breakdowns of The Knockout, this winter’s smash-hit crime drama.

I honestly can’t tell whether this is the singularity finally arriving,

or, like blockchain and the metaverse before it, just another feeding frenzy for investors.

While everyone else is busy trolling ChatGPT, we, as an account devoted to acoustics, naturally wanted to know what the breakthroughs behind it mean for our field. Which is how we came across the video below.

Color me a little stunned, especially by the Morgan Freeman at the end.

That bass voice—

I wouldn’t say it’s exactly the same,

it’s just completely indistinguishable!

And it works in real time! Real time!

How do you turn into someone else, say Elon Musk? Gao Qiqiang?? An Xin! An Xin! (Gao and An are the gangster and the cop at the heart of The Knockout.)

The software above, Voice_AI, offers a way. You can’t change who you are, but you can change how you sound. The technology is known as voice cloning.

Let’s hope scammers don’t get hold of it. Someday a friend may call, and the person on the other end of the line may not be your friend at all. Followers of this account, please spread the word and warn the people around you: scammers are often the first to master new technologies, and a new kind of scam call may well be on its way.

Some people use the software to turn into Musk, and Musk uses it himself; in fact, it turns out Musk was the one promoting it in the first place. There’s video to prove it:

Which raises the question: why would he promote it for free? A little digging gives the game away. “Iron Man” Musk was an early investor in OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT, so of course he talks up his own wares, to make sure whoever takes the stake off his hands pays a good price.

And who is that buyer?

That’s right: good old Uncle Microsoft, a seasoned buyer of other people’s bets! As you’ve probably seen, Uncle Microsoft has already built ChatGPT 3.5 into the Edge browser and Bing search.

Back in the day, Brother Google’s Chrome stomped Uncle Microsoft’s IE into the dirt and beat it into what became Edge, while Bing has always languished in the “others” column. But Uncle Microsoft never gave up on them. He waited, waited for his chance to turn the tables, and finally it came. This time he wants to take out Brother Google’s search and browser in one go.

Brother Google hastily fielded Bard in response, but alas, Bard came up a little short and Google lost 170 billion dollars in a single day. Ouch. Google’s products really are great to use. A year or two ago, when Meta started going downhill, I still thought Google’s moat was deep enough to keep it on top for many years to come. Who knew Uncle Microsoft wouldn’t bother building a bridge across the moat? He just borrowed a plane and airdropped straight into the city!

Who gets the last laugh is anyone’s guess. The rest of us will keep munching popcorn.

Rome wasn’t built in a day, and Uncle Microsoft is a buyer with a conscience: he has already invested one billion dollars in OpenAI and is set to invest another ten billion. Early this year he also came out with a model called VALL_E, which can do what Voice_AI above does.

The research has been published too, and the real highlight is the author list below!!! Notice anything?

In the end, the tech race is a race for talent!!!
